sections.html:
Martin Howard founded Hello New Home, and he lives in Somerset. From Taunton to Bath, the person taking the photographs, showing the viewings, handling move-in and move-out and writing each quarterly inspection report is the man who started the company. Switch agent and he meets your tenant at the handover. Your calls come to him.

He knows who rents here and why. Hinkley Point C brings contractors to the Bridgwater area. Musgrove Park Hospital and the county offices bring staff to Taunton, Leonardo Helicopters to Yeovil, and Bath has its two universities. Then come the M5 commuters heading for Bristol. He founded Property Predator, which analyses rents, yields and deals, and mentors property investors, so his rent advice is worked out, not guessed.

Contracts, deposits and rent collection run from head office in Swansea under client money protection, and your agreement is with Hello New Home. WhatsApp Martin on 07510 243096 or ask for a free rent review.

Three things bring Somerset landlords to us. The Renters' Rights Act, which rewrote every tenancy in England on 1 May 2026. An agent in Taunton or Yeovil charging a percentage, then renewal, inspection and notice fees, with a 12-month tie-in. And a Hinkley Point C contractor asking for six months, which the agent cannot price.

Our answer is 12% of the rent, capped at £150 a month, no VAT added, no renewal, inspection or notice fees, and 30 days' notice to leave. The written statement of terms, the landlord database paperwork and the licence check are part of management. And the person who inspects your house is Martin, who lives here.

sections.h2: Somerset rents and what 12% costs here
sections.html:
The ONS average private rent for the Somerset Council area was £1,016 a month in August 2026, up 6.2% on the year. At £1,016 our fee is £122 a month. Bath and North East Somerset averaged £1,885, and North Somerset about £1,209, which is £145.

Our cap of £150 starts at a rent of £1,250. In Bath that is most of the city: a £1,885 flat pays £150, not the £226 a straight 12% would be. In Taunton, Yeovil or Bridgwater it takes a larger family house to reach it; a two-bed pays 12% with nothing added.

A county average covers a Chard terrace and a Bath townhouse alike. The free rent review prices your house against lets on your street.

sections.h2: Licensing in Somerset: mandatory HMO, nothing selective
sections.html:
Somerset Council runs mandatory HMO licensing: five or more people from two or more households sharing a kitchen, bathroom or toilet need a licence, and letting without one can mean a civil penalty of up to £30,000. We found no additional or selective scheme in the Somerset Council area in October 2026, and we confirm every address before marketing.

Bath and North East Somerset is mandatory licensing only; its additional scheme ended on 31 December 2023. North Somerset licenses HMOs on the same five-person test. If you let by the room, hellomyroom, our shared-house team, manages the licence, fire safety and room lets together.

sections.h2: The towns and who rents them
sections.html:
• Taunton: the county town, with Somerset Council at County Hall and Musgrove Park Hospital, the county's largest acute hospital with about 700 beds. Long lets to hospital, council and professional households.
  • Bridgwater: about 12,000 people were on the Hinkley Point C site at peak construction in May 2025, and many of them rent nearby. The Agratas battery factory planned at Gravity, with up to 4,000 jobs, follows.
  • Yeovil: Leonardo's helicopter site employs nearly 2,800 people. Long lets to engineering households and contractor stays by the month.
  • Wells, Glastonbury and Street: a cathedral city, the town below the Tor, and Clarks Village, which brings up to 4 million visitors a year to Street.
  • Frome and Shepton Mallet: long lets to households working in Bath and the Mendip towns, with Worthy Farm and Glastonbury Festival three miles from Shepton Mallet.
  • Weston-super-Mare and Clevedon: M5 junctions 21 and 20, with stations on the line into Bristol. Commuter long lets all year, seafront short stays in summer.
  • Bath: 21,685 students at the University of Bath, Bath Spa University alongside, and the highest rents in our area.

sections.h2: How the Local Partner model works in Somerset
sections.html:
Martin Howard founded Hello New Home and lives in Somerset, so the Local Partner here is the founder. He does the photographs, viewings, move-ins, move-outs and quarterly inspections, takes your calls, and meets your tenant at the handover when you switch agent. He also runs Somerset Lettings, Hello New Home's sister agency in the county. If you already let through Somerset Lettings, ask Martin how the two fit together.

Everything regulated runs from the office: the agreement and written statement of terms, Right to Rent checks, deposit protection, rent collection, the repairs desk, the compliance calendar and any licence application. We belong to a redress scheme and a client money protection scheme, both named on our fee sheet, and your agreement is with Hello New Home.

If you know your patch and want to open the next town, the Local Partner programme explains how.

Ask for a free rent review. Send the address and we call within one working day with a realistic rent for your street, the licensing position, and a written comparison of our 12% against what you pay now. If you own a flat in Bath, a Cheddar cottage or a Bridgwater house contractors ask about, the free short-let appraisal gives you both figures side by side. Martin will bring either in person.

faqs.q: What does full management cost in Somerset?
faqs.a: 12% of the monthly rent, capped at £150, with no VAT added and no extras. On the Somerset average rent of £1,016 that is £122 a month. On a Bath flat at £1,885 it is the £150 cap. Tenant Find on its own is £495, no let no fee.

faqs.q: Does my Somerset property need a licence?
faqs.a: Only if it is an HMO: five or more people from two or more households sharing a kitchen, bathroom or toilet. Somerset Council and Bath and North East Somerset run mandatory HMO licensing only as of October 2026, and we confirm the position with the relevant council for every address before marketing.

faqs.q: Who looks after my property day to day?
faqs.a: Martin Howard does, in person. He lives in Somerset and handles the photographs, viewings, move-ins and move-outs, the quarterly inspection with a written report, and your calls. Contracts, deposits, rent collection and compliance run from head office in Swansea under a redress scheme and client money protection, and your agreement is with Hello New Home, so the paperwork never rests on one person.

faqs.q: What changed for Somerset landlords on 1 May 2026?
faqs.a: The Renters' Rights Act came into force in England. Tenancies are periodic, section 21 has gone, rent can rise once a year by notice, and a written statement of terms is required before the tenancy is agreed. The landlord database opens from 15 December 2026, and we prepare your entry with you. We handle the rest.

faqs.q: Which parts of Somerset do you cover?
faqs.a: The TA and BA postcode areas, so Taunton, Bridgwater, Minehead, Yeovil, Wells, Glastonbury, Street, Frome, Shepton Mallet and Bath, plus BS21 to BS29, BS39, BS40, BS41, BS48 and BS49 for Clevedon, Weston-super-Mare, Cheddar, Nailsea, Yatton and the Chew Valley. If you are unsure, send the postcode.

sections.h2: The Renters' Rights Act, done for you
sections.html:
Since 1 May 2026 every tenancy in England is periodic. Fixed terms are gone, section 21 is gone, and possession runs on the Section 8 grounds. Rent can go up once in any 12 months by a Section 13 notice with two months' notice, and the tenant can take it to the tribunal. You cannot take more than one month's rent in advance, and a tenant's request to keep a pet needs an answer within 28 days.

Before any tenancy is agreed the tenant must have a written statement of the key terms; missing it carries a fine of up to £7,000. We serve it with the agreement. From 15 December 2026 the private rented sector database opens and every landlord in England will need to register; we prepare everything the registration asks for and walk you through it when your region's window opens; the entry is made in your name.

If you ever need the house back to live in or to sell, Grounds 1 and 1A need four months' notice and cannot be used in the first 12 months of a tenancy. We tell you the earliest real date rather than the one you were hoping for.

Your tenant does not need to move for you to. We give notice to your current agent, collect the deposit certificate, the gas and electrical certificates and any licence, check the file against the Act, and Martin meets the tenant at the house. If a gas certificate has lapsed or the written statement was never served, you hear about it before we take over, not after.

faqs.q: Is the 12% fee really the whole cost?
faqs.a: For management, yes: 12% of the monthly rent, capped at £150, no VAT, no renewal, inspection or notice fees. Set-up is £295, waived when you switch an existing tenancy to us. Rent guarantee is optional at £25 a month. On a £1,016 rent you pay £122 a month.

faqs.q: Do you do Right to Rent checks?
faqs.a: Yes. Every adult who will live in the property is checked before the tenancy starts, as England requires. The office runs the check and keeps the record; Martin collects the documents in person where that is easier for the tenant.

faqs.q: Can I still get my property back if I need it?
faqs.a: Yes, on the grounds the Renters' Rights Act allows. If you or close family need to move in, or you want to sell, Grounds 1 and 1A need four months' notice and cannot be used in the first 12 months. We advise on timing before you decide.

faqs.q: What does the rent guarantee add-on cover?
faqs.a: It is a named insurance product, added to Full Management for £25 a month, that covers unpaid rent subject to the policy's conditions, which include the tenant passing referencing. We show you the policy wording before you add it. It is not a promise that rent arrives whatever happens.

faqs.q: How quickly can you take over a managed property?
faqs.a: Usually within the notice period you have with your current agent. We handle the notice, the deposit and file transfer and the paperwork check, and Martin introduces himself to the tenant. Tell us your agent's notice period and we work to it.

shortlets.h1: Airbnb and short-let management in Somerset
shortlets.intro: Somerset has a summer, a festival week, a cathedral city, a seaside and a power station being built, and a quiet season in between. We run long lets and short lets here from the same team, so we can tell you what your Bath flat or Cheddar cottage nets as a short let and as a tenancy, after every cost, using local occupancy by month. Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue.

sections.h2: What drives short stays in Somerset
sections.html:
Exmoor National Park recorded 1.6 million tourism visits in 2024. Cheddar Gorge and the Mendips draw visitors all year. Glastonbury Festival's licence allows up to 210,000 people on site at Worthy Farm, three miles from Shepton Mallet, in late June. Bath has 21,685 students at the University of Bath alone, plus Bath Spa, and visitors all year. Weston-super-Mare, Burnham-on-Sea and Minehead have a summer season and a quiet winter.

About 12,000 people were on the Hinkley Point C site at peak construction in May 2025, and many of them rent nearby, so a Bridgwater house let by the month to a contractor earns in January as well as July. Musgrove Park and Leonardo in Yeovil bring relocation stays of a month or more.

A flat in Chard or a village house on the Levels will not book like one in Bath. If your address is in the wrong place for short stays, the appraisal says so and quotes the long let.

Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue, with cleaning passed through at cost. It covers pricing by season, guest vetting and messaging around the clock, cleaning and linen, restocking, repairs, reviews, a monthly owner statement and the night-count tracker. SA Co-Host is 12% for owners who run their own cleaner and want pricing, listing and guest messages handled. SA Launch is £495 for photography, listings on Airbnb, Booking.com and a direct-booking page, pricing rules, a house manual and the compliance pack, and is waived with 12 months of Full SA Management. No VAT is added, and you can leave on 30 days' notice.

sections.h2: Business rates, council tax and the register
sections.html:
Business rates or council tax. In England a self-catering property is rated as a business only if it was available to let for 140 nights and actually let for 70 nights in the past 12 months. Below that it pays council tax, and since 1 April 2025 Somerset Council has charged a 100% premium on furnished homes that are no one's main residence: double council tax for a short let that misses the test. Bath and North East Somerset and North Somerset set their own; we confirm the position for your address.

The register. The government says a national short-let register for England will be running by March 2027. We will register your property when it opens.

Safety. Fire risk assessment, gas and electrical certificates, PAT testing and an insurance check are in the SA Launch compliance pack. This is the list we work to, not legal advice.

sections.h2: One team, three ways to let
sections.html: A Bath flat can take short stays through the summer and a tenancy from September. A Bridgwater house can go to a Hinkley contractor for three months, then to a family. Flex Switch moves a property between short stays, contractor and relocation lets of a month or more, and tenancies, with the same agent, the same owner statement and no re-onboarding. A national co-host cannot take a property back as a long let; a high-street agent will not run it as a short let. We do both, and Martin meets the cleaner, checks the changeover and answers the door.

sections.h2: Next step: the free short-let appraisal
sections.html: Request the free short-let appraisal with your address. You get the long-let figure and the short-let figure side by side, net of platform fees, cleaning, utilities, voids and management, plus the rates test and council tax position in writing. If the long let wins, the figure is the one the free rent review gives, and we manage it at 12%.

faqs.q: Will my Somerset short let pay business rates or council tax?
faqs.a: Business rates only if it was available for 140 nights and actually let for 70 in the past 12 months. Otherwise council tax applies, and Somerset Council has charged a 100% premium on second homes since 1 April 2025. Bath and North East Somerset and North Somerset decide their own. Our tracker reports your night count monthly.

faqs.q: How much do you charge to manage a short let in Somerset?
faqs.a: Full SA Management is 18% of net booking revenue, cleaning at cost. SA Co-Host is 12%. SA Launch is £495, waived with 12 months of Full SA Management. No VAT is added and there is no 12-month minimum.

faqs.q: Which parts of Somerset suit short stays?
faqs.a: Bath first, for the universities and visitors all year. Cheddar, Exmoor and the coast in the summer season. Bridgwater and Taunton for contractor stays by the month. Most villages and the smaller towns earn more as long lets, and the appraisal will say so if that is true of yours.

faqs.q: Can you let my house to Hinkley Point C contractors?
faqs.a: Yes. Contractor and relocation lets of a month or more are part of Flex Switch, priced by season and by demand on the site. We vet the company and the occupiers, and when the contract ends the house can go to a tenancy with the same agent. We quote both figures before you decide.

faqs.q: Can I switch between short let and long let?
faqs.a: Yes. Flex Switch is included: a property can move between short stays, monthly lets and a tenancy with us and no re-onboarding. A tenancy is managed under the long-let fee, and the owner statement stays the same.
